text: This is a real bug report. In TiddlyWiki, Ctrl+Enter stopped saving your work.
Somewhere in a hundred and sixty-one commits, one change broke it.
One person in the thread suspected a commit. Undoing it didn't help.
Gumshoe reads the report, and writes one plain sentence to test. No test code. No selectors.
Kane CLI opens the app in a real browser. An older version works. The version in the report is broken.
So Gumshoe tests the commit in the middle.
Eighty left.
Kane does the steps, and looks at the screen, the way a person would.
Forty.
Twenty.
Ten.
Five.
Three.
One.
Found it.
One commit, out of a hundred and sixty-one. Seven tests. Thirty-two minutes.
Then we checked it without any AI. A plain script agrees. And the commit people suspected? The bug was already there before it.
We ran the same check twenty more times. Ten works. Ten broken. Every single time.
Claude Code writes the fix. It can't see the maintainers' fix, and it can't touch the test.
Kane runs the same sentence. It works. And the sentence is saved as a Kane test.
Kane doesn't get the last word. A second reader sees only the screenshot. If they disagree, the test is thrown out. Never guessed.
Seven searches, on real bugs. None planted. Every time the maintainers named a commit, Gumshoe found the same one.
And you can watch every search on the live page.
Gumshoe. Paste a bug report. Get the commit that broke it.
